The data filter does not prevent denial-of-service attacks. Availability of extraction filters should be checked with hasattr(tarfile, 'data_filter') rather than a Python-version comparison.

Path.absolute() makes the path absolute without normalization or resolving symbolic links. Path.resolve() eliminates double-dot components. When resolve(strict=False) encounters a missing path, it appends the unresolved remainder without checking whether that remainder exists.

Since Python 3.13, a symlink loop raises no exception in non-strict resolve mode. Path.lstat() reports the symbolic link itself rather than its target. Each Path.stat() call looks up a fresh result.

Path.is_file() propagates permission errors. Passing follow_symlinks=False to Path.exists() checks the symlink itself.

mutations.before: Path.absolute() makes the path absolute without normalization or resolving symbolic links.
mutations.after: Path.absolute() normalizes the path and resolves symbolic links.
mutations.reason: Transfers resolve behavior to absolute; two separately atomized errors.

mutations.after: Since Python 3.13, a symlink loop still raises RuntimeError in non-strict resolve mode.
mutations.reason: Transfers the explicitly historical RuntimeError behavior into the new non-strict branch.

mutations.after: Path.is_file() converts permission errors to False.

cases.baseline_answer_before_controlled_mutati:
For a type implementing Drop, Rust calls Drop::drop before recursively destroying its fields. Struct fields are dropped in declaration order. Variables captured by move in a closure have unspecified drop order. Assignment destroys an already-initialized left-hand operand.

When control leaves one drop scope, its variables are dropped in reverse declaration order. Leaving nested scopes at once drops variables from the inside outward. A function parameter is dropped after bindings introduced by that parameter’s pattern.

Within a pattern, variables are dropped in reverse declaration order. For an or-pattern, binding order comes from the first subpattern even when the second subpattern matches.

mutations.before: Struct fields are dropped in declaration order.
mutations.after: Struct fields are dropped in reverse declaration order.
mutations.reason: Confuses field destruction with local-variable destruction.

mutations.reason: Transfers struct-field ordering to scope-local variables.

Ignored tests are still compiled in test mode, and the harness can force their execution with --include-ignored. The expected text in should_panic is matched as a substring of the panic message. A test carrying should_panic must return ().

cases.baseline_answer_before_controlled_mutati:
An object’s owner is normally the role that created it. Granting a privilege to PUBLIC grants it to every role. Referencing existing column values in UPDATE requires SELECT privilege.

An owner may revoke their own ordinary privileges, but can always grant them back because ownership retains grant options. A blank Access privileges column means built-in default privileges; an explicit (none) means no ordinary privileges are granted even to the owner. Functions and procedures receive PUBLIC EXECUTE by default.

In the ACL example calvin=r*w/hobbes, calvin has SELECT with grant option from hobbes.

mutations.reason: Adds an unmentioned audit retention policy.
